name: Celanese
description: Celanese makes two kinds of products. Engineered Materials sells specialty plastics (nylon, polyacetal, liquid crystal polymers, elastomers, UHMW polyethylene and others) to carmakers, medical, electronics and consumer-goods manufacturers, mostly by working with a customer on a project and pricing on the value to that customer. The Acetyl Chain sells acetic acid, vinyl acetate monomer, emulsions and EVA polymers (the building blocks of paints, adhesives and coatings) and acetate tow, which goes mostly into cigarette filters; these are priced more like commodities. In November 2022 it bought DuPont's Mobility & Materials business with borrowed money and still carried $12.6 billion of debt at the end of 2025; it cut its quarterly dividend about 95 percent from the first quarter of 2025 and wrote off $1.1 billion of goodwill and $346 million of trade names in Engineered Materials in 2025. Engineered Materials lost $958 million at the operating line in 2025 while the Acetyl Chain earned $539 million.

businessLines.name: Engineered Materials
businessLines.how: Project-based sales to carmakers, medical and electronics makers and their molders under multi-year and annual arrangements; price is set on value-in-use and is generally independent of raw material cost, so margins widen or narrow as input costs move; equity affiliates add earnings and dividends.
businessLines.description: Engineering thermoplastics and elastomers: EAE, EVA pharmaceutical copolymers (VitalDose), LCP, long-fiber reinforced thermoplastics, nylon, POM, polypropylene compounds, TPE, thermoplastic polyesters, TPV and UHMW-PE, plus 17 strategic affiliates.
